items.headline: Strait of Hormuz stays near-closed as four tanker attacks hit in 48 hours
items.summary: Commercial transits are running near 1 a day against a pre-crisis baseline of about 85. Some LNG cargoes crossed in September, but attacks on crude and LNG tankers on 28–29 Sept renewed supply fears.
items.rationale: A prolonged closure keeps energy prices and war-risk insurance high. Energy-importing Asia and Europe take the largest cost shock; the US, a net exporter, is partly cushioned. Gulf exporters lose volume but gain on price.

industries.why: Rerouting, war-risk premiums and jet-fuel costs
Higher realised prices for producers outside the Gulf
Fertiliser and feed inputs move through the Gulf

economies.why: Imports most of its crude, much of it via Hormuz
Heavy reliance on Gulf crude and LNG
LNG and diesel prices pass through to inflation
Large importer, partly hedged by stockpiles
Export volumes capped despite high prices
Net energy exporter gains on terms of trade

items.headline: Brent holds near $97–103 as global oil inventories fall 400 million barrels this year
items.summary: Brent is up about 49% from a year ago. OPEC+ is expected to keep output targets unchanged, and forecasters raised their 2026 average Brent estimate to about $89.
items.rationale: Oil near triple digits feeds headline inflation and keeps central banks hawkish. Producers benefit; fuel-heavy sectors and oil-importing economies lose.

industries.why: Strong cash flow for producers and oil services
Fuel is the largest variable cost
Fuel and goods inflation curbs discretionary spending
Fuel costs dampen demand for larger vehicles

economies.why: Higher price per barrel exported
Shale output gains; consumers pay more at the pump
Oil import bill weighs on the rupee and the deficit
Import bill rises with a weak terms of trade
Energy inflation keeps policy tight
Higher input costs for manufacturers

items.headline: US Federal Reserve raises rates to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike since 2023
items.summary: The 12–0 decision cited inflation that has been too high for too long, with core PCE near 3.2%. The median projection signals one more quarter-point hike this year.
items.rationale: Tighter US policy lifts borrowing costs worldwide and firms the dollar. Rate-sensitive sectors suffer most; bank lending margins widen, but loan demand and credit quality become risks.

industries.why: Higher discount rates compress growth valuations

economies.why: Slower housing and credit growth
Portfolio outflows pressure the rupee
Dollar pegs import tighter US policy
Imported tightening through gilt yields

items.headline: Global bond selloff pushes the US 30-year yield to 5.53%, highest in over 20 years
items.summary: The US 10-year yield reached 5.22%, a 19-year high. UK 30-year yields trade near 5.74% as energy-driven inflation spreads across developed markets.
items.rationale: Long-term yields set the cost of mortgages, corporate debt and government borrowing. High term premiums hit long-duration assets and leveraged sectors, and expose banks holding long bonds to mark-to-market losses.

industries.why: Cap rates and mortgage rates reprice higher
Long-duration earnings are worth less today

economies.why: Deficit financing gets more expensive
Gilt yields among the highest in the G7
Spreads widen for high-debt members
Global yields pull on Japanese bond markets
Global yield pull draws funds from local bonds

items.headline: European Central Bank lifts its deposit rate to 2.50% as the energy shock raises inflation
items.summary: Staff projections see euro-area inflation averaging 3.0% in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027, with conflict in the Middle East the main source of price pressure.
items.rationale: Hiking into an energy shock protects inflation expectations but weighs on credit-dependent growth. European lenders gain margin; housing, autos and household demand cool.

industries.why: Lenders earn more on deposits and loans

economies.why: Slower credit and consumer growth

items.headline: Bank of England holds at 3.75% in a split 6–3 vote as UK inflation heads toward 4%
items.summary: UK CPI rose to 3.1% in August and is projected near 3.75% in Q4 and above 4% in early 2027. The Bank set a path of £20 billion a year in active gilt sales.
items.rationale: Holding while peers hike gives UK borrowers short-term relief, but the inflation overshoot keeps a hike likely. Sterling and gilts stay sensitive to every move in energy prices.

economies.why: Persistent inflation squeezes real incomes

items.headline: Bank of Japan raises its policy rate to 1.25% in a 7–2 vote
items.summary: The quarter-point increase continues Japan's exit from ultra-low rates while inflation stays above target.
items.rationale: Higher Japanese rates support domestic lenders and the yen. A firmer yen trims exporters' overseas earnings when converted home, but it also lowers Japan's energy import bill.

industries.why: A firmer yen trims exporters' earnings

economies.why: Tighter financial conditions for a fragile recovery

items.headline: US and China cut tariffs on about $30 billion of each other's goods and extend their truce to 10 Jan
items.summary: About 90% of covered products drop to most-favoured-nation rates. US cuts cover toys, appliances, baby and household goods; China's cover farm products, personal care, medical devices and coal.
items.rationale: Lower tariffs cut costs for importers ahead of the holiday season and reopen Chinese demand for US farm goods. The truce lowers near-term trade-war risk, but it expires in January.

industries.why: Cheaper imported household goods before peak season
Chinese buyers return for US farm products

economies.why: Export relief for consumer-goods factories
Lower import costs and farm export demand

items.headline: China's factory index returns to growth at 50.1 as new property support lands
items.summary: The manufacturing PMI rose from 49.8, ending two months of contraction, and construction activity expanded for the first time this year. New measures target first-time buyers and cut a policy lending rate to 1.5%.
items.rationale: Steadier Chinese construction supports demand for steel, copper and machinery and helps commodity exporters. The property support is targeted, so the recovery may stay modest.

industries.why: Steel and copper demand from construction
Targeted relief for first-time buyers in China

economies.why: Factories and construction back above 50
Machinery and component exports to China
Capital-goods exports to China

items.headline: AI server demand drives another round of memory-chip price increases into Q4
items.summary: DRAM contract prices are forecast up 10–15% quarter on quarter and NAND flash up 15–20%. Leading memory producers hold under 10 days of inventory, and global chip sales hit a record $425 billion in Q2.
items.rationale: Chip producers and equipment suppliers hold the pricing power. Device makers, carmakers and consumer electronics face rising component costs that squeeze margins or lift shelf prices.

industries.why: Record pricing for chips and AI infrastructure

economies.why: Home to most AI-infrastructure spending
Chip equipment and materials suppliers
Domestic AI-chip makers raise prices

items.headline: Fertiliser costs set to rise more than 30% this year as Gulf shipping disruption tightens supply
items.summary: Urea topped $850 a tonne in April, its highest since 2022. Wheat futures are up about 12% since late February, and fertiliser-intensive crops face the largest cost increases.
items.rationale: Higher input costs squeeze farm margins now and food prices later. Food-importing and subsidy-heavy economies carry the most fiscal and inflation risk.

industries.why: Food inflation follows with a lag
Fertiliser producers outside the Gulf gain pricing power

economies.why: Bigger fertiliser subsidy bill and food inflation
Higher farm input costs
Food inflation adds to energy pressure

items.headline: Indian rupee trades near 96 per dollar, down over 8% in a year, as the central bank intervenes
items.summary: Dollar sales and swaps by the Reserve Bank of India have drained nearly $20 billion of rupee liquidity. A firm dollar, high crude and US 10-year yields above 5.2% keep pressure on the currency.
items.rationale: A weaker rupee raises the cost of fuel and component imports but makes India's services and generic-drug exports more competitive. Tighter liquidity lifts local borrowing costs.

industries.why: IT-services exporters earn more per dollar
Tighter rupee liquidity lifts funding costs

economies.why: Imported inflation and capital outflows

items.headline: German business confidence hits its highest since 2023 while consumer sentiment slumps
items.summary: The Ifo index rose to 89.9, its fifth straight increase. The forward-looking consumer climate indicator fell to −30.6 for October.
items.rationale: Factories report recovering orders, but households squeezed by energy costs are cutting back. The split favours exporters and capital goods over retail and services.

economies.why: The industrial core regains momentum

items.headline: Japan's carmakers face $14 billion more in US tariff costs as the EU weighs favouring EU-built EVs
items.summary: US tariffs and policy shifts cost Japan's six largest carmakers nearly $28 billion in one fiscal year. A proposed EU industrial law would favour electric vehicles built inside the bloc.
items.rationale: Trade barriers are splitting the global car market into regional blocs. Producers with factories inside each market gain; export-led manufacturers lose margin.

industries.why: Tariff costs and fragmented EV rules

economies.why: Car exports are a core earner
EV exports face new EU barriers
Local EV production would be favoured

items.headline: Gold rebounds to about $4,185 an ounce after weak US data trims rate-hike bets
items.summary: Prices remain well below January's record near $5,590 but rose 1.4% as softer data lowered the odds of further Fed tightening.
items.rationale: Gold is acting as a gauge of rate expectations. The rebound helps miners and signals that markets doubt how far the Fed will go.
